newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks flat as deregulation delayed again.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks flat as deregulation delayed again.

text.p: Jakarta stocks were flat at midday on Friday as the government announced that an economic deregulation package had been postponed to next week, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index was down 0.66 points, or 0.09 percent, at 734.83 points at the lunch break. Advancers led decliners by 51 to 43 with 54 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 221 billion rupiah.
"It's Friday and the market is usually rather slow due to shorter trading hours because of prayer time," one broker said.
Poultry firm Sierad Produce was the most active, with some 60 million shares traded on market talk that the share price was expected to touch 1,000 rupiah, brokers said.
Sierad fell 75 rupiah to 850 rupiah after touching a day high of 975 rupiah due to late profit-taking, they said.
One analyst with a local brokerage firm said Sierad's fundamentals were not very promising due partly to weak DOC (day old chicken) prices.
"There was also market talk that the firm would focus more on expanding its fast food network, but the recent sharp hike in Sierad was mostly due to speculative reasons," she said.
